extracted.intended_audience: communication scholars, academic researchers, oral-history readers, and scholars interested in academic teaching/research practice
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted guidance and evaluative principles about academic teaching, seminar design, research and writing practices, and collaboration as described in an oral-history interview with a communication scholar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach what you do
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson of the Annenberg School is that you teach what you do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course offerings should reflect the instructor's research strengths and interests (e.g., technology, politics, political influence). Teaching alignment with one's scholarship provides authenticity and leverage for course content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer small graduate seminars
rubrics_metrics.description: A small group that I could intervene with. A small group that had to write papers. A small group that did essay exams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small graduate seminars allow close interaction, meaningful interventions, sustained writing assignments, and partnership-style mentorship; these features are often missing in large undergraduate classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students as partners and collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students are partners in this process; you are collaborators in this process. Students introduce me to something I hadn’t looked at in the past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat graduate students as collaborators who can bring new literatures and ideas. Practices include negotiated independent studies where both advisor and student read the same material and return to discuss it, leading to mutual learning and sometimes co-authored publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate teaching constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Undergraduate teaching often involves big courses with limited opportunity for deep interaction; undergraduates are less likely to write essays or take essay exams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use teaching assistants to manage large classes, but recognize that undergraduates typically provide less of the collaborative, publication-oriented payoff that graduate mentoring yields; faculty may prefer multiple smaller graduate classes over large undergraduate teaching loads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seminar purpose: exposure to diverse scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: If it’s not for credit, it is supposed to expose you to other people’s positions and understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-credit or funded seminar series should bring in external scholars to broaden participants' perspectives; successful seminars often result in speakers and ideas appearing in participants' later publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize research materials digitally (use searchable PDFs and topical buckets)
rubrics_metrics.description: I use files in the computer. Now I have PDF files... I can write on them, underline them, and I can search and find things on PDFs... I have a number of different buckets—an inequality bucket and a race bucket and a production bucket and a policy bucket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain topical digital folders ('buckets'), capture and annotate articles (including news hyperlinks), and rely on full-text search to retrieve notes and prior judgments when drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline-driven project construction
rubrics_metrics.description: I have an outline. I need to get to an outline. What are the sections of this book or of this project?... Outlines in Microsoft Word are not fixed devices, they are adjustable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a flexible outline that defines sections and components; move, reorder, or remove sections as the argument develops; use the outline as the insertion point for sourced material from files/buckets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative research as publication-focused teamwork
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost everybody on that team was committed to that project and was going to make a contribution to that product and hope they got paid off by not a grade, but by a publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat collaborative projects as team efforts with publication as the primary reward; set shared commitments and expectations for contribution and authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book review method
rubrics_metrics.description: There’s almost a formula for writing a book review... read the book and you think about it, and you say, Alright, this is what I want to say about this. And there’s almost a formula for writing a book review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the book thoroughly, develop a clear evaluative thesis, and support that thesis with selected examples from the book; follow a consistent structure when producing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use experimental framing to test effects on participation
rubrics_metrics.description: We did something that approximates an experiment. It assigns people to groups and asks the questions in slightly different ways, so one can see about the framing of the question, how it influences their responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying attitudes or participation (e.g., willingness to join genetics research), use between-group framing manipulations to observe causal effects of presentation and question wording on responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seminar funding increases scholarly impact
rubrics_metrics.description: This seminar, funded by the university for four years... was beneficial for me in terms of introducing me to so many people that I later cited in my work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure funding for recurring seminar series to bring in national/international speakers; sustained, funded seminars enhance networks and increase the likelihood that participants’ work will cite and build on visitors' ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use current media and hyperlinks as research leads
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York Times has become ... a major source of my reading, because of the articles filled with hyperlinks. Someone will make reference to something and provide a hyperlink and I’ll capture it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor trusted news outlets for linked sources and follow hyperlinks to primary material; capture and file these items for later annotation and integration into research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about naming endowed chairs after living persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Nobody said anything. I mean, nobody gave me advice and said, You’re not supposed to put somebody’s name in when he’s living. But I did.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anecdotal institutional norm: avoid naming professorships or chairs after living individuals without prior consultation; consider seeking advice about conventions before proposing a named position.
